content.title: About
content.content: Processed cheese is a product made from cheese, milk, cream and food additives that undergoes heat treatment. American singles are commonly used in sandwiches, burgers and snacks. They have a soft texture, melt easily when heated, and feature a mild buttery flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Processed cheese was first developed in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to extend cheese shelf life.
Singles are often packaged in stacks of 12–24 slices for convenient portioning.
Emulsifiers such as sodium phosphate are added to achieve a uniform meltable texture.
The cheese melts quickly, making it popular for sauces, toppings and baked dishes.
In the U.S., processed cheese is classified as a distinct food category separate from traditional cheese.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Processed cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Each serving supplies a notable amount of protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product contains vitamins B2 and B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Heat processing makes the proteins more readily absorbable.

items.title: Convenient portion size
items.content: Single slices allow quick addition of a cheesy flavor without extra preparation.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed cheese often contains a lot of salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Emulsifiers and preservatives may cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or casein allergy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Singles are relatively calorie‑dense, so they should be consumed in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Single slices are perfect for hot sandwiches, burgers, on top of potato wedges, in macaroni and cheese, or simply melted in the microwave for a quick snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–7 °C in the original packaging. After opening, reseal tightly to prevent drying out. Shelf life is typically 3–4 weeks.
